The model has two hinge joints (shoulder at planar_reach.xml:27, elbow at :32) and two motors (shoulder_motor gear 2.0 and elbow_motor gear 1.5 at :47-50), with a 0.002 s RK4 step at :3; the bridge derives action.ctrl's per-actuator bounds from the motor ctrlranges of -1 to 1 (the default motor class at :8 and both elements at :48-49), so the package writes no Limit of its own and declares no operator-required bound. The fake backend is fake.py, a callable stand-in mujoco module: it parses the same MJCF for the step, the two hinge coordinates and the two ctrlranges and gears, then integrates a placeholder first-order motion; its only invented constants are marked '# placeholder'. Expected simulator-family warnings only: G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake is the stand-in mujoco module, not a package class surface) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (the family-derived inputs seed, ticks and action.ctrl[*]); G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warning. NOT COVERED: MuJoCo was not installed where the gate runs and was never run, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result; the stand-in computes no inertias, contacts, friction, damping, armature or RK4 integration. The bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from zero qpos/qvel, not from the upstream environment's reset (env.py:116-117 draws the joint positions from -0.35 to 0.35 rad and the velocities from a normal distribution with scale 0.02, and env.py:195-206 samples and writes a target the bridge never moves). The upstream environment's 12-number observation (env.py:49-51), reward shaping (env.py:227-235) and 0.035 m success threshold (env.py:35, :144) are not served; cap.world.step.v1 returns the bridge's {time, qpos, qvel} observation and the world state {time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed}. No rendering, camera, viewer or sensor stream is served, and no physical arm is modelled or driven; snapshot/restore is advertised through the bridge's integration state but is not covered by the CL3 gate. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six cases (model shape, per-actuator control-range refusals, state follows the control target, reset to model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch), all passing. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null): no human review and no hardware run are claimed.
